domain: pharmacovigilance - adverse drug reaction reports (Canada Vigilance database)
prediction_question: Hypothetical task this source would support: predict the outcome or seriousness of a reported adverse drug reaction (patient demographics, suspect drug, reaction) from the Canada Vigilance reports - the Canadian counterpart of FAERS/openFDA-style tasks. Also considered at reopen: suspect-drug role identification (DRUGINVOLV) within multi-drug reports.
prediction_time: Would be the report's initial receipt by the Canada Vigilance Program (DATINTRECEIVED), with seriousness/outcome as resolved in a pinned extract vintage - stateable on the reopen evidence below, but moot given the drop reason.
target_definition: Not fixed: report-level seriousness or outcome class (OUTCOME_CODE, SERIOUSNESS_CODE + six criterion flags). Moot given the drop reason.

measurements.task_family_comparison: Carried over and now decisive: the US counterpart (FDA FAERS via openFDA) ships event-level ADR data through a documented anonymous API, and the exact task shapes are published and mirrored - see rejection_reason.
measurements.reopen_path_closure_2026_10_30: Full-archive pass over reports.txt (the entire 422,306,974-byte member) via bounded range fetches - 8 requests x 4 MiB covering the member's whole 32,884,931-byte compressed span plus a 128 KiB central-directory tail and a HEAD; output discarded, aggregate counters only, nothing retained. Measured 2026-10-30: 1,154,017 rows, all 42 fields, 0 bad rows; 0 duplicate-adjacent REPORT_ID rows and 0 non-increasing ID transitions (file strictly sorted by REPORT_ID), i.e. exactly ONE row per REPORT_ID across the whole archive - the extract carries NO per-version rows, so the recorded reopen condition ('multiple VERSION_NO rows per REPORT_ID -> follow-up/outcome-revision task') is measured FALSE. VERSION_NO is a per-report version/follow-up count: 0=810,975 (70.3%), 1=178,622 (15.5%), 2=63,226, 3=29,751, 4=17,157, 5=11,213, tail to 16+. Follow-up (VERSION>=1) rate by DATINTRECEIVED year: 0% pre-2000, 1-2% 2001-2006, 26-43% from 2008 (system change), 2024 35.8% (right-censored; 2022 43.8%, 2023 42.3%). Seriousness col25 mix: 01=781,425 / 02=372,592. Same session: extracts page (modified 2026-10-23, via extraction backend) confirms monthly update cadence, coverage 1965 to 2026-06-30, current ZIP ~344 MB at www.canada.ca/content/dam/hc-sc/migration/hc-sc/dhp-mps/alt_formats/zip/medeff/databasdon/extract_extrait.zip; the CKAN resource remains the 20241130 vintage. Probe scripts retained at probe/ (vig_probe1.py central-directory + grain preview, vig_probe2.py prefix sample, vig_probe3.py full-archive aggregate pass).

rejection_reason: DROPPED (mirror) on the standing novelty test after the access premise was corrected and the candidate reopened. The natural tasks this source carries already exist in published/ML-ready form on the open US analogue: (1) GCAP, Communications Biology 2023 (s42003-023-05243-w): a released benchmark of 141,752 drug-ADR interactions with seriousness labels in the same 7-class FDA scheme (DE/LT/HO/DS/CA/RI/OT), built from FAERS + ADReCS with splits - report/drug-interaction seriousness prediction; (2) ISPOR 2025 (CTIME meeting poster): FAERS serious-outcome classification on 242,312 case-molecule observations using the identical feature shape this extract offers (age, sex, reporter type, indication bucket, molecule identity, MedDRA PT indicators; ROC-AUC 0.916); (3) Kaggle/GitHub FAERS seriousness pipelines (e.g. 528k-report serious-outcome predictors with released code) and openFDA's anonymous report-level API itself; (4) the suspect-drug identification variant is also published: Frontiers in Pharmacology 2026, 'Expert-Referenced Evaluation of Large Language Models for Primary Suspect Drug Identification in the FAERS Database' (LLM vs expert reference standard). A Canadian re-issue would change the jurisdiction, publisher and drug population, not the task - the same standing test that dropped hc-recalls-classification (US analogue prior art) and hc-cannabis-inspection-rating (same task, different jurisdiction). The 2026-10-21 secondary concern ('even unparked, differentiation would be uphill') is thereby resolved as a rejection, with the access facts corrected so no future tick re-parks this source on the wrong premise.
next_action: None - dropped (mirror), and the recorded reopen path is now CLOSED by measurement (2026-10-30): the full-archive pass above shows reports.txt carries one row per REPORT_ID, not per-version rows, so the follow-up/outcome-revision task is not constructible from this extract. A 'will a follow-up arrive' task on VERSION_NO is also not viable: the extract publishes only the LATEST version's attribute values (DATRECEIVED='latest' per the publisher's schema), so initial-receipt-time features beyond DATINTRECEIVED do not exist in it, and the version count for recent reports is right-censored. Do not reopen on this extract; a publisher-side per-version export (or a dated historical-vintage archive) would be a NEW candidate with its own novelty check.
